brief: BEA revisions lowered recent core PCE readings (July revised down 35bp to 3.0% y/y, September printed 3.0%) due to methodological changes in three hard-to-measure categories. BofA argues this does not change the underlying inflation story, which it still estimates at 2.5% y/y with no improvement over the past year, because Chair Warsh weighs the trajectory of underlying inflation over the headline level. Risks to that trajectory remain tilted to the upside from AI-driven hyperscaler capex (projected +90% y/y this year, +36% next year), energy shortages tied to the Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, pockets of labor-market tightness concentrated in AI and data-center wages, and resilient consumer demand. Therefore BofA continues to expect the Fed to take a risk-management approach and tighten policy at its remaining two meetings this year, with next week's FOMC minutes watched for how much disagreement exists over further tightening. Separately, GDP growth was revised up (2Q to 2.2%, 1Q to 2.5%), lifting BofA's 2026 forecast to 2.3%. The bank also sees midterms as unlikely to change the growth and earnings backdrop, and it is turning more bullish on the consumer, flagging a budding lower-income spending rebound.
